prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1196; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the claimant, who reports a low-speed collision while the vehicle was parked and backing out of a stall in a shopping center lot.

Entry 2: Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the loss.

Entry 3: Requested photos of the vehicle and the lot from the claimant. Photos were received and show damage consistent with a rear-quarter impact.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account matching the claimant's description of how the two vehicles came together.

Entry 5: Police report reviewed. The responding officer lists the claimant as an occupant of the vehicle, and two independent witnesses are named in the report.

Entry 6: Obtained statements from both witnesses, who confirm the collision happened as described and that the claimant was in the driver's seat.

Entry 7: Claimant reports a knee injury from the impact and has started a course of treatment with a provider of their choosing. Treatment notes requested.

Entry 8: Reviewed the damage estimate. The repair scope is mostly in line with the impact the photos and statements describe. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the prior claims search.

Entry 9: Treatment notes received. The injury fits the kind and force of the crash, and care followed a usual course, easing off as the claimant improved.

Entry 10: Claimant disclosed a small strain to the same area several years ago that healed fully. Nothing in the file suggests the current injury was caused by anything other than this collision.

Entry 11: Claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far. Nothing points to damage predating the start of coverage. Claim is progressing to settlement review.
